Beyond this workshop: curated external skill collections

View source on GitHubLast updated 3 November 2026

On this page
  1. How to install a skill (general)
  2. The collections
  3. What we learned, and what we did not adopt

The ten skills in this repository cover one review workflow with the human in charge. Many other skill collections exist, some with tens of thousands of GitHub stars. This page lists the ones we reviewed on 3 November 2026 for evidence synthesis (systematic, scoping and literature reviews, appraisal, reporting), with what they do well and what to watch for. Stars, licences and last updates come from the GitHub search API on that date; they change quickly.

Warning

Read before you install. A skill is not a document: it is a set of instructions that steers your agent, often with scripts the agent will run on your machine with your permissions. A third-party skill can run code, send your files to external services, ask for API keys that cost money, or tell the agent to ignore your instructions.

  • Read every SKILL.md, reference file and script before installing. If you cannot read the code, do not install the skill.
  • Prefer official or well-maintained sources, and pin a release or commit (for example gh skill install ... --pin <tag or SHA>) so that the content cannot change under you.
  • Install into one project folder (.claude/skills/) to try it, not into your personal skills for every project.
  • Be wary of skills that need API keys, install packages, call paid services, or promise an "autonomous" or "end-to-end" review. None of them removes your responsibility for every decision.
  • Check the licence before you copy or adapt anything, and the data-protection rules of your institution before any skill touches unpublished or personal data.
  • Beginners: as for the rest of this workshop, external skills are for learning only. Do not use them to conduct a real review.

How to install a skill (general)#

Method Command or step Notes
Claude Code plugin marketplace /plugin marketplace add <owner>/<repo>, then /plugin install <plugin>@<marketplace> Documented by Anthropic for anthropics/skills (/plugin install example-skills@anthropic-agent-skills or document-skills@anthropic-agent-skills) and by many repositories below. Anthropic's own marketplace: /plugin marketplace add anthropics/claude-plugins-official (Claude Code docs)
Copy a folder cp -r <skill-folder> .claude/skills/ (this project) or ~/.claude/skills/ (all your projects) Works for any skill that follows the Agent Skills specification; you see exactly what you install
Installers npx skills add <owner>/<repo>, gh skill install <owner>/<repo> [skill] --pin <ref> Convenient, but they run code and may install many skills at once; prefer pinning
claude.ai Upload a packaged skill in Settings (Customise, Skills) Only name, description, license, compatibility, metadata and allowed-tools are accepted in the frontmatter

htlin222/meta-pipe 150 Academic and non-commercial licence 2026-09-23 End-to-end meta-analysis pipeline (screening, extraction, R analysis, manuscript) showing how far automation can be pushed Sold as "end-to-end automation"; dual AI screening counted as dual review; model-reported confidence used to triage extraction; API keys; restrictive licence Clone and set up as its README describes
keemanxp/slr-prisma 117 MIT (licence file; GitHub shows "other") 2026-03-28 Walks through writing a review section by section against the PRISMA 2020 items; explains records, reports and studies Drafts the whole manuscript, introduction and discussion included, with citations; it checks references by web search, but a real reference can still be attached to a claim it does not support .skill file from its Releases page (claude.ai, Customise, Skills), or copy the folder
BESSER-PEARL/research-agent-skills 18 MIT 2026-10-20 research-paper-review: structured critique, checks for numerical inconsistencies Written for computer-science papers; not a systematic-review tool npx skills add BESSER-PEARL/agent-skills@research-paper-review (as written in its README)
lingzhi227/agent-research-skills 448 none 2026-02-27 deep-research: six-phase literature review with phase gates (each phase must leave files on disk) No licence (no reuse); the skill points to an API-key file on the author's own computer; AI/CS literature focus Its README uses an install.sh: read it before running anything

What we learned, and what we did not adopt#

Strong external skills improved ours (see THIRD_PARTY.md): treating record text as data rather than instructions, piloting with known eligible studies, PABAK next to kappa, a human re-check of records both AI runs excluded, checking direction and magnitude of a claim and not only the presence of a quote, and an automatic check of PRISMA flow arithmetic.

We deliberately did not adopt:

  • "Autonomous" or "end-to-end" reviews. Several popular collections run search, screening, extraction, risk of bias, GRADE and writing with few human checkpoints. Guidance expects human oversight and responsibility (Cochrane-Campbell-JBI-CEE position statement 2025, doi:10.1186/s13750-025-00374-5).
  • Two AI passes reported as dual review, and model-reported confidence scores used to decide what humans check.
  • AI-generated risk-of-bias or GRADE ratings. Our new skills collect the evidence and draft; humans judge.
  • Manuscript drafting with citations by the AI, because of the risk of invented or misattributed references.
  • Paid APIs, installers and very long skills (over 1,000 lines), which make a skill hard to read and to audit in a workshop.

To add a collection to this page, or to report that an entry changed, open an issue.
